scope: Resolve the P0 external-blocker predecessor named by current donor stern.py: exact archived wache-koenig.py + freigabe source, classify what it actually blocks, and constrain Frankenstein-2.0 EffectGate migration without granting current runtime reachability.

atoms.what_it_does: Reads a PreToolUse-style JSON event, ignores every tool except Bash, classifies the shell command, exits 2 for hard-deny classes or ticket-required commands lacking a valid ticket, and exits 0 otherwise.
atoms.why_it_exists: Provide a real blocking boundary for selected destructive shell commands rather than post-hoc journaling.
writes: deletes ticket on expiry or successful consumption
dependencies: hook scheduler must interpret nonzero PreToolUse hook exit as blocking
atoms.authority_class: historical blocking Bash-command gate if and only if installed in the live hook scheduler
atoms.failure_mode: It provides zero coverage for non-Bash tools by design; scheduler absence or bypass removes its enforcement entirely.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Ticket is consumed by unlink before command execution, giving simple single-use behavior; no explicit cross-process lock around exists/read/unlink is present.
atoms.privacy_implication: Exact command text is hashed; stderr can echo up to the first 300 characters of a blocked command in the suggested human freigabe command.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Pure local parsing/file lookup on normal path.
runtime_entrypoints: historical/global PreToolUse scheduler, exact current installation not proven in this run
tests_or_receipts: archive receipt DRIVE-AICORE-AUTH-005 contains a safe non-executing classifier replay; not new runtime evidence
known_counterevidence: Current Frankenstein donor stern.py explicitly calls this an older separate blocking watcher, but current donor repo does not contain the watcher or its global settings.json installation.
open_questions: Recover exact hook scheduler/settings identity and ordering for the historical installation.
Determine whether any separate current gate covers Write/Edit/NotebookEdit and other non-Bash state-changing tools.

atoms.what_it_does: Strips heredoc/string data before primary pattern checks, anchors destructive patterns at command positions, reinspects ssh/scp/rsync and bash/sh/zsh -c inner commands, hard-denies device formatting/raw writes, and ticket-gates destructive/delete/system-path/database/history-rewrite patterns.
atoms.why_it_exists: Reduce false positives from destructive words appearing in data while still catching nested executed command strings.
atoms.authority_class: historical classifier feeding the blocking Bash hook
atoms.failure_mode: Regex/text parsing cannot establish semantic completeness across all shell equivalences, interpreters, encodings or indirect side effects; it must not become the final EntityOS capability semantics.
tests_or_receipts: Historical safe replay: benign mentions free; delete/nested destructive ticket; formatting hard deny.
known_counterevidence: Source explicitly exempts /tmp/claude-* scratch and admits self-modification by the same user unless protected by host ownership/mode.
open_questions: Convert useful cases into typed intent/resource/capability regression fixtures rather than regex authority.

atoms.what_it_does: Loads a ticket named from the command SHA-256 prefix, verifies the full command hash and validity window, and unlinks the ticket before returning allow so a successful grant is one-shot.
atoms.why_it_exists: Bind human approval to one exact destructive command and prevent reusable blanket approval.
atoms.failure_mode: Binding is to exact command text, not a canonical typed effect/resource object; path identity, resolved executable identity, environment, cwd and indirect resources are not cryptographically bound by this ticket format.
atoms.concurrency_implication: No explicit atomic create/consume primitive beyond filesystem unlink; race behavior should not be assumed safe without measurement.
atoms.privacy_implication: Ticket stores exact command text locally.
atoms.state_lifetime: 10-minute delayed activation + 20-minute validity window, single use
open_questions: Successor should bind typed effect intent, resource identity, generation, owner grant identity and execution lease atomically rather than raw command string alone.

atoms.what_it_does: Requires /dev/tty, two sequential fresh typed challenges, timing heuristics, optional deletion-size bound, then writes a mode-0600 one-shot command-hash ticket with delayed activation and expiry.
atoms.why_it_exists: Keep the AI tool invocation from self-approving a destructive command by requiring a separate human-operated terminal path.
reads: target paths for optional size measurement
atoms.failure_mode: Typing-speed heuristics are not an identity proof; the stronger property is separation via a real controlling TTY. It intentionally does not stop a deliberate human.
atoms.privacy_implication: Stores exact command in local ticket.
tests_or_receipts: archive receipt classifies this as DIRECT_SOURCE_OWNER_GATE_MECHANISM
open_questions: Replace behavioral typing heuristics with explicit authenticated owner/capability grant while preserving out-of-model separation, scope binding, expiry and single use.

hypotheses: Frankenstein-2.0 should preserve the architectural split discovered here: candidate/model requests never self-authorize; a deterministic host/executor boundary consumes a separately minted owner/capability grant before execution.

The raw-command one-shot ticket is a useful donor for capability-lease semantics, but the successor should bind a canonical typed EffectRequest + resource identity + generation + exact executor identity rather than shell text.
The current stern journal can sit behind the successor gate as observation/provenance, but its ZUGELASSEN/VERIFIED labels must not be the enforcement decision.
counterhypotheses: A different current host-level permission layer may already supersede wache-koenig and cover more than Bash; if exact source and live scheduler evidence establish that, adapt the newer gate instead.

Command-text tickets may be simpler and safer than a larger typed effect object for shell-only use; this must be tested against aliasing, cwd/environment/resource resolution and multi-tool execution before migration complexity is justified.
contradictions: TW5-CONTRADICTION-EFFECT-SEMANTICS-002 REFINED: current stern.py normal admission bookkeeping is nonblocking, while the exact historical wache-koenig source is genuinely blocking for selected Bash commands when installed. These are two different authority classes and must not be merged into one 'EffectGate' label.

TW5-CONTRADICTION-WACHE-REACHABILITY-004 OPEN: stern.py names the older global watcher, and archive evidence preserves its exact source, but this run has not recovered the exact current/historical global settings.json scheduler binding for wache-koenig itself. Source capability therefore does not equal current runtime reachability.

TW5-CONTRADICTION-WACHE-COVERAGE-005 OPEN: wache-koenig exits immediately for non-Bash tools. It cannot by itself establish one complete real-effect authority for Write/Edit/NotebookEdit or non-shell tool effects.
critical_unknowns: Exact global settings.json or equivalent scheduler entry that invoked this wache-koenig snapshot, including hook ordering relative to any other PreToolUse hook.
Whether current Frankenstein 0.7 runtime still inherits this exact watcher, a successor watcher, Claude host permissions, or no equivalent host gate.
Whether all state-changing tool classes converge on one deterministic execution boundary; current evidence says no such convergence can be credited from stern.py + wache-koenig alone.
Atomicity of ticket consumption under concurrent identical command attempts is unmeasured.

recommended_next_spans.reason: Prove actual hook registration/order and matcher scope for wache-koenig.
Trace realtime function-call/tool executor permission boundary and compare it against hook-based Bash gating.
Determine actual present execution authority for Write/Edit/Bash and whether a single gate exists.
Convert command-bound one-shot owner-grant cases into typed EffectRequest/capability regression fixtures.
